pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as three to four kettlebell sessions a week, reduced to two or three to work around dialysis days, plus five to fifteen minutes of daily mobility. He tied it straight to his own stated deficit rather than just agreeing: 'I don't see any problem with that, and I actually welcome the fact that there's a program that is going to be put together without me just making stuff up as I go along, you know, not knowing if I'm doing things right or wrong.' He had already named self-programming as the thing he cannot do. No concern was raised by either party about performing loaded ballistic work with an indwelling dialysis catheter.

The only pillar he interrogated. He compared it against his own experience of P90X ('I felt like I was eating all day... it's unsustainable') and keto, corrected his own terminology mid-sentence with the rep's help ('Ketoacidosis? Is that the word?' / 'Ketosis'), and then raised the clinical constraint himself: 'the only thing we have to factor in is that there is a kidney, certain things you can and cannot... you got to be cautious as to how much of certain things that you eat, like potassium and stuff like that.' The rep answered a different question — that ketosis was not required — and the potassium point was not returned to. Note the protocol was described without the rep ever having asked what the prospect eats.

This is the pillar he came for and he named it before it was presented: 'you don't have to convince me that this is something I need to do or that I want to do. I want to do it. I just need, at this point in my life, I need somebody there to go, all right, Craig, you know, let's get busy.' He explicitly framed the CrossFit community as what he lost — 'there were people there to motivate and to have camaraderie, but I don't have that anymore' — and the rep sold the community back to him in exactly those terms ('see it like CrossFit, like people are just training together'), noting the presence of members in their forties, fifties and seventies. Response: 'All right' and 'Yeah, I'm with you.'

anchors.raw: I've committed to $2,000 for her program. But I'm going to, I have to do that in increments. You know, I can't just come out and lay it all out at one time.
anchors.note: The most important anchor on the call and it was never treated as one. He has already committed a third of the Primal price to a practitioner promising a cure for the underlying condition, is paying it in instalments, and ranks it ahead in his own budgeting ('I have to parcel out, you know, for you, for her'). It competes for the same money and for the same hope, and the rep neither contested it nor accounted for it.

anchors.raw: I'm on a fixed income, and I earn about $2,000 a month... right now I have about 400 bucks to my name... I have medical bills out the [wazoo]
anchors.note: A hard ceiling, disclosed twelve minutes before the price was presented. A $1,200 monthly instalment against a $2,000 monthly disability income is sixty per cent of gross before medical bills, care costs and the competing Ayurvedic payments. This is not an objection to be handled; it is an arithmetic disqualification.

anchors.raw: if it comes through, then the talk of money will be no problem. I'll be a wealthy man. But I'm, we usually, right now we're trying to get a withdraw done... it hasn't materialized yet.
anchors.note: The only supportive anchor and it is unrealised, unverifiable and long-running — he has been investing six years, has three positions, and is stuck trying to complete a withdrawal. He set his own deadline: 'I will have to know by the end of August, if things haven't gone my way, then I'm going to shelve the projects.' The entire follow-up plan rests on this. Flagged rather than counted as genuine buying power.

anchors.raw: I know how to do the CrossFit, and we have a CrossFit box here in Gillette. And P90X is something I can do at home on a computer. I'm just intrigued with kettlebells.
anchors.note: He has two known, cheaper, immediately available options he has succeeded with before, and says the draw to kettlebells is curiosity rather than necessity. What he actually lacks is not a modality but supervision and a reason to show up, and neither of the alternatives supplies that either — which is the real case for the offer and was never made in those terms.

anchors.raw: I haven't been on a proper holiday for about six years, and I'm trying to go down to see a buddy of mine in Florida for a couple of weeks, and so I'm trying to budget for that... I do have a strong desire to go to the Philippines, I want to do some diving.
anchors.note: Two trips being budgeted for out of the same $2,000 a month, one of them around his birthday on 2 September, which is also when the second follow-up checkpoint was set.

unmet_demand.want: Training that is safe and appropriate during in-centre haemodialysis with an indwelling catheter, and that might reduce post-dialysis disequilibrium — his single most specific ask: 'I'm hoping that this can help me overcome those days of dialysis where I don't feel so bad.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nobody on the call could answer it and nobody said so. The rep's response to whether it would work was 'There's only one way to find out if that's going to work. And that's to do it', and he later encouraged attempting mobility work on dialysis days on the basis that 'it's going to help you overall'. No clinician was consulted, referenced or suggested. Whether this programme is appropriate for this prospect at all is unknown.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition protocol compatible with renal dietary restriction — he raised potassium limits himself and noted there are things he must be cautious with.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The protocol as described is generic whole foods with an emphasis on fibre, vegetables and adequate protein, plus time-restricted eating — a pattern that intersects directly with potassium, phosphate and protein restrictions typical in dialysis. The rep answered a different question and moved on. This is not a positioning gap that better wording would close; a renal diet is a clinical prescription the offer does not provide.

unmet_demand.want: A price he can fund on $2,000 a month of disability income while already paying $2,000 in instalments to another provider.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Only the $6,000 programme was offered, and only in the six-instalment $7,200 form. The $200/month tier this rep presented to another prospect the previous day was never mentioned. He was sent a free video and told to buy his own kettlebell.

unmet_demand.want: Someone to hold him to it through the three-to-four month point where he has abandoned every previous programme — 'I need somebody there to go, all right, Craig, let's get busy.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Genuinely served by the accountability pillar and correctly sold back to him. Recorded because the interim plan inverts it exactly: he was told to buy a kettlebell and train from a video alone, with no coach and no community, for at least six weeks — the precise condition under which he has said his whole life he stops.
